s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute respiratory and systemic illness in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Subjective fevers, shortness of breath, and worsening cough for 6 days
key_facts: 50-year-old man
Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) with intravenous immunoglobulin every 3 weeks
HIV with undetectable viral load, CD4 count 140 cells/µL on therapy
Chronic bronchiectasis with history of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary infection
Recurrent giardiasis
Myopathy treated with long-term low-dose prednisone
Recurrent herpes simplex virus infections
Oxygen saturation 97% on room air
CD4 count: 140 cells/µL
HIV viral load: Undetectable
Viral resistance testing showed mutations in UL97 and UL54 genes
Serial CMV viral load measurements showed increasing levels

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Increasing CMV viral load measurements and immunocompromised state

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: History of Pneumocystis prophylaxis and immunocompromised state

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
shortlist.why_kept: History of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary infection and chronic bronchiectasis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of immunodeficiency and increasing CMV viral load measurements, which suggests a CMV infection. The presence of viral resistance testing showing mutations in UL97 and UL54 genes further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient is on trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis prophylaxis, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
rejected.why: There is no recent evidence of this infection, and the patient has a history of treatment for it

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of this infection in the provided information

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not suggest Guillain-Barré syndrome, and the focus is on respiratory symptoms
